title: Redwood Dedicated: Throughput Tiers (Standard / Performance / Premium)
author: Kira Thompson
body:
## Overview
Redwood Dedicated provides reserved, isolated inference capacity with enforceable throughput guarantees and tiered operational policies.

This page defines the **customer-facing tier semantics** (Standard / Performance / Premium), including:
- Included features and operational controls
- Supported hardware shapes per tier
- Regional availability constraints
- Throughput guarantees (what we guarantee, how we measure, and what is excluded)
- Burst, overload, and maintenance policies

**Audience:** Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, SRE, and Customer Success.

---

## Definitions (used across all tiers)
### 1) Primary throughput guarantee metric
**Guaranteed Sustained Throughput (GST)**
- **Metric:** *Effective output tokens per second* (output tok/s)
- **Aggregation:** **p50** of output tok/s over a **5-minute rolling window**, evaluated continuously
- **Scope:** Per **Dedicated deployment** (single customer + single region + pinned model version + specific shape)

**What “effective output tok/s” means:** Tokens counted after request admission, measured at the gateway/runtime boundary, excluding tokens that are not part of successful model output (see exclusions).

### 2) Eligibility / workload envelope (what the guarantee assumes)
The GST guarantee applies when the deployment is operating within the tier’s defined workload envelope:
- **Pinned model/version** from the Dedicated-supported catalog for the chosen shape
- **Max input context (p95):** within the model/shape’s published max for the tier (see “Tier matrix”)
- **Streaming:** allowed; measurements include streaming tokens that are successfully emitted
- **Concurrency:** within the tier’s documented sustained concurrency envelope
- **Safety features enabled:** Redwood-provided admission control and overload protections must remain enabled

If a customer’s workload regularly exceeds envelope assumptions (e.g., highly spiky concurrency, frequent max-context prompts, or unusually long outputs), the correct resolution is **tier/shape resizing** or a **workload-specific sizing engagement**, not disabling guardrails.

### 3) Measurement exclusions (not counted against GST)
The following time and traffic are excluded from SLO accounting and tier guarantees (full list in the Measurement Standard):
- Planned maintenance windows (per tier policy below)
- Deployment warmup/rollout windows (initial bring-up, canary cutovers)
- Customer-induced errors (4xx), invalid requests, or requests blocked by customer-configured safety rules
- Customer traffic exceeding documented envelope (e.g., context length cap exceeded)
- Force majeure / upstream cloud region-wide outage

### 4) What happens when GST is at risk
All tiers use **admission control/backpressure** to preserve service health. When overload is detected, Redwood may:
- Throttle new requests (429 / “capacity_exceeded”) rather than allowing latency collapse
- Reduce allowed concurrency to maintain stability
- Temporarily disable burst (if enabled) to protect sustained performance

**Important:** Expected throttling under overload is **not automatically an SLO breach**. An SLO breach occurs when the system is within the documented envelope but still fails the GST objective per the SLO definition.

---

## Tier matrix (customer-facing semantics)
The tiers differ in (a) the **strength of the throughput guarantee**, (b) **tail-latency guardrails**, (c) **burst behavior**, and (d) **operational rigor** (maintenance, support response, reporting).

### Summary table
| Category | Standard | Performance | Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target customer | Predictable baseline Dedicated capacity | Latency/throughput-sensitive production workloads | Mission-critical workloads with strongest guarantees + strict ops |
| GST objective (p50 output tok/s over 5m) | **>= 0.75×** published baseline for pinned model+shape | **>= 0.85×** published baseline | **>= 0.90×** published baseline |
| Tail-latency guardrail (informational) | p95 E2E latency tracked, best-effort | p95 E2E latency tracked + alerting | p95 E2E latency tracked + tighter alerting + escalation |
| Sustained concurrency envelope (guidance) | Up to **8** concurrent streams per GPU-equivalent (workload dependent) | Up to **12** concurrent streams per GPU-equivalent | Up to **16** concurrent streams per GPU-equivalent |
| Burst policy | Optional, limited | Included | Included + higher ceiling |
| Burst ceiling (above reserved) | Up to **1.2×** for short intervals | Up to **1.3×** for short intervals | Up to **1.5×** for short intervals |
| Overload behavior | Throttle first; protect stability | Throttle with earlier signals + proactive comms | Throttle + proactive mitigation (capacity shift where available) |
| Autoscaling | Optional (shape-dependent) | Supported for eligible shapes | Supported + priority scheduling |
| Reporting | Basic dashboard + weekly export | Dashboard + daily export | Dashboard + daily export + monthly SLO report |
| Support | Standard Support | Priority Support | Enterprise Support + named escalation path |
| Change/maintenance | Standard windowing | More restrictive windows | Most restrictive windows + advance notice |

**Notes**
- “Published baseline” refers to Redwood’s internal benchmark baseline for the chosen **model+shape+region**, updated periodically. The baseline is not a promise; the **GST ratio** is the promise.
- For customers who require absolute numeric guarantees (e.g., “>= X tok/s”), see **Exception Policy** below; this requires finance + SRE approval and is only supported on Performance/Premium.

---

## Included features by tier
### Standard
Included:
- Dedicated, isolated GPU capacity in a single region
- Pinned model version and rollout controls (canary + rollback)
- Basic observability: throughput, throttling rate, saturation signals
- Default admission control + overload mode enabled

Not included / limited:
- Burst is optional and subject to region/shape availability
- No priority access to constrained shapes during supply shortages

### Performance
Everything in Standard, plus:
- Burst included (when supported by region/shape)
- Expanded sustained concurrency guidance (see matrix)
- More aggressive internal alerting on throughput regression
- Eligibility for additional shapes (A100 80GB, H100 PCIe) where available

### Premium
Everything in Performance, plus:
- Highest GST objective (ratio to baseline)
- Highest burst ceiling (subject to fleet constraints)
- More restrictive maintenance policy and proactive comms
- Priority handling during fleet contention events (within contract constraints)
- Optional dual-region failover add-on (availability varies; not part of base tier)

---

## Supported hardware shapes (by tier)
Shape availability varies by region and supply. Final provisioning is subject to fleet confirmation.

### Shape naming
Shapes are referenced as:
- `rw-ded-<gpu>-<count>-<mem>-<interconnect>` (examples below)

### Standard: supported shapes
- `rw-ded-l4-1x-24g` (single node, no NVLink)
- `rw-ded-l4-4x-24g` (single node, PCIe)
- `rw-ded-a10-4x-24g` (single node, PCIe) *(limited availability)*

Constraints:
- MIG is **not** supported for Dedicated tiers (Dedicated uses full-GPU isolation).
- Standard shapes are optimized for cost efficiency and predictable baseline throughput; not recommended for very large models or extreme tail-latency requirements.

### Performance: supported shapes
- All Standard shapes, plus:
- `rw-ded-a100-1x-80g`
- `rw-ded-a100-8x-80g-nvlink`
- `rw-ded-h100-8x-80g-pcie` *(region-limited)*

Constraints:
- For multi-GPU nodes, NVLink is required for the `a100-8x` shape.
- Multi-node is supported only via approved cluster shapes (below) and requires customer workload qualification.

### Premium: supported shapes
- All Performance shapes, plus (where available):
- `rw-ded-h100-8x-80g-sxm-nvlink` *(high demand; region-limited)*
- `rw-ded-h100-8x-80g-sxm-nvlink-ib` *(for cluster configurations)*
- Approved cluster shapes (Premium only):
  - `rw-ded-h100-sxm-8x` **x2 nodes** (IB/RoCE required; model dependent)

Constraints:
- Premium shapes may require longer lead times and have explicit regional restrictions.

---

## Regional availability constraints
Availability is reviewed monthly and can change due to GPU supply.

### Standard
- Generally available in: **us-east-1**, **us-west-2**, **eu-west-1**
- L4 capacity is typically available with shorter lead times

### Performance
- Available in: **us-east-1**, **us-west-2**, **eu-west-1**, **eu-central-1** (shape-dependent)
- A100/H100 PCIe availability may be quota-limited

### Premium
- Limited availability in: **us-east-1**, **eu-central-1**
- H100 SXM capacity is tightly controlled; Premium may be temporarily “waitlist” in some regions

**Contracting rule:** If a tier is sold in a region where Premium shapes are not currently provisionable, the order form must state “subject to fleet confirmation” and specify approved fallback shapes or a lead-time commitment.

---

## Burst policy (all tiers)
Burst is intended to absorb short demand spikes without requiring permanent overprovisioning.

### Burst semantics
- Burst is defined as temporary capacity above the reserved sustained envelope.
- Burst is **best-effort** and **not part of GST** (GST is evaluated on sustained throughput within the reserved envelope).
- Burst may be reduced/disabled automatically during fleet contention or when stability signals indicate risk.

### Burst limits by tier
- Standard: up to **1.2×** (optional)
- Performance: up to **1.3×** (included)
- Premium: up to **1.5×** (included)

### Burst eligibility (shape-dependent)
Burst is generally supported on single-node shapes. Multi-node/cluster shapes require explicit approval.

---

## Overload + admission control behavior (what customers should expect)
When the deployment approaches saturation, Redwood enforces tier-specific backpressure to maintain reliability.

### Standard overload mode
- Primary action: **throttle new requests**
- Goal: prevent latency collapse and protect ongoing streams
- Customer-visible signal: 429 capacity errors + “retry_after” guidance

### Performance overload mode
- Same as Standard, plus:
  - earlier warnings surfaced in customer dashboards
  - on-call receives pre-breach alerts for sustained queue depth

### Premium overload mode
- Same as Performance, plus:
  - proactive mitigation attempts when available (e.g., shifting within pre-approved capacity pools)
  - tighter escalation path and comms expectations

---

## Maintenance and change policy
Maintenance policy impacts availability and measurement exclusions.

### Standard
- Maintenance windows allowed with standard notice
- Planned maintenance excluded from throughput SLO accounting

### Performance
- More restrictive maintenance windows; higher notice expectation

### Premium
- Most restrictive maintenance windows
- Advance notice required except for urgent security patches
- Customer Success notified proactively for any impactful changes

---

## Customer-visible reporting
All tiers provide customer access to Dedicated metrics via the Console and export.

Minimum required panels (all tiers):
- Effective output tok/s (5m rolling)
- Throttling rate (429)
- Queue depth / saturation signals
- Request/stream concurrency

Exports:
- Standard: weekly export available
- Performance: daily export available
- Premium: daily export + monthly SLO summary

---

## Tier selection guidance (internal)
Use this when helping customers pick a tier.

Choose **Standard** when:
- Workload is steady and cost-sensitive
- Customer can tolerate occasional throttling during spikes

Choose **Performance** when:
- Workload has material peakiness and needs higher sustained concurrency
- Customer is latency-sensitive and wants stronger guardrails and alerting

Choose **Premium** when:
- Throughput predictability is business-critical (revenue-impacting)
- Customer requires strongest ratio-to-baseline guarantee and strict operational posture
- Customer is requesting advanced mitigation options and priority handling

---

## Exception policy (absolute throughput numbers, non-standard shapes, or region overrides)
Non-standard commitments (e.g., “>= 120k output tok/s sustained” or “Premium in a non-supported region”) require:
- Product approval (Dedicated DRI)
- SRE approval (error budget and enforceability)
- Fleet approval (capacity feasibility)
- Finance approval (pricing uplift)
- Legal review (order form/SLA language)

**Rule of thumb:** Exceptions are only considered for **Performance** or **Premium**, and must include explicit workload assumptions and the measurement reference.

---

## FAQ
**Q: Why are guarantees expressed as a ratio to a baseline instead of a single number?**
A: Throughput varies materially by model architecture, context-length distribution, output length, and streaming. Ratio-to-baseline guarantees remain enforceable while allowing Redwood to publish updated baselines per model/shape as runtimes evolve.

**Q: Is throttling a breach?**
A: Not necessarily. Throttling is an expected protection mechanism under overload. A breach is evaluated per the SLO definition when the system is within the workload envelope but fails GST.

**Q: What should Sales put in the order form?**
A: Reference the tier (Standard/Performance/Premium), the provisioned region, the shape(s), and the throughput SLO measurement reference. Use Legal’s approved language for any custom commitments.
